ruling.explanation:
Rider: the deviation on this trip is established but excused, and the one charge that should never have reached you is returned.

The GPS trace records 11.18 km driven against the 8.2 km booked optimal — an excess of 2.98 km and 36.34%, over both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km, 20%). But the LTA advisory ADV-20260714-031 (EV-ADVIS-00103-01) records an all-lane emergency closure of Braddell Road between Lorong 1 Toa Payoh and Bishan Rd — exactly the corridor your optimal route uses — active 05:30–12:00 and overlapping your 08:07–08:36 trip, with intersects_route and overlaps_trip_window both true. Under POL-RD-03 the justified excess is min(2.98, 1.30 x (10.6 - 8.2) + 1.00 = 4.12) = 2.98 km, i.e. the whole excess, so the diversion is FULLY exonerated and the distance and time charges stand. POL-RD-02 therefore does not run: it applies only where no exculpatory clause fully excuses the excess, and POL-RD-03 excuses all of it here. The $4.15 in the fare breakdown's closure branch is not applied — it is the POL-RD-02 recomputation against the closure-adjusted optimum, and the $0.15 above the ERP is the distance/time differential that stays with the driver. The driver drove the closure-adjusted optimal: 8.2 + 2.98 = 11.18 km, matching the trace's 11.18 km.

What you do get back is the ERP. Both gantries charged — CTE (Braddell Rd towards City) $3.00 and CTE (Moulmein Rd towards City) $1.00, total $4.00 — are flagged on_optimal_route=false, and your booked optimal route carries no ERP at all (optimal_route_erp_sgd 0.0). Under POL-RD-09(2), where a deviation is exonerated as an external event under POL-RD-03, the distance and time charges stand but off-route ERP is refunded to the rider as a standalone pass-through correction, capped at $12.00 per trip. $4.00 is inside that cap, so $4.00 is returned. Your 'ok' to the driver's 'braddell close today, i take CTE ah' does not turn this into a rider-requested detour: no rider instruction names a road or a waypoint and waypoint_hint is null, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable and POL-RD-09(3) does not take the refund away from you.

Driver: your routing is upheld and you keep the distance and time charges; you are not penalised for a diversion the closure required. Both gantry charges are genuine crossings — the trace passes within 0.0 m and 40.2 m of them, well inside the 250 m match — so this is not a billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4), and no billing-integrity referral arises. No POL-RD-06 repeat pattern exists (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 553, and the excess is not material at 36.34% / 2.98 km against the 50% / 8.0 km marks), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral. POL-RD-04's compensation limb does not fire either: you were billed 11.2 km against a trace of 11.18 km, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall. The only money moving is the $4.00 off-route ERP pass-through, which you never keep.

The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (175 fixes at a 10 s interval, coverage 100%, empty gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0), so POL-RD-07 does not fire, and no POL-RD-10 escalation trigger is engaged: the trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and every charge line has a counterpart. No artifact in this ruling carries a weight below 1.0, so confidence is not capped.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of $4.00 off the $25.12 charged.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Decision on trip TRP-00104 (Tampines Hub to one-north), for both parties.

WHAT THE TRACE SHOWS. The GPS trace measures 34.17 km and that is the figure that governs the threshold test (POL-RD-01; the trip record's 34.2 km is a rounded copy and may not be cited). The booked optimal route was 27.1 km. The excess is 7.07 km, or 26.09% of optimal, which clears both POL-RD-01 gates (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km), so the deviation is established on this trip's own measurement. It does not reach either materiality marker (50% or 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; and in any event the driver's trailing-90-day record is 1 flag in 288 completed trips, far below the pattern thresholds, so no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral can follow. The lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and is not substituted. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (283 fixes, 10-second sampling, 100% coverage, no gaps), so POL-RD-07's corroboration rule and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route are not open, and the excess is measured directly.

THE DRIVER'S EXONERATION. POL-RD-03 applies. LTA advisory ADV-20260716-007 (HIGH severity, two of three lanes blocked) names the PIE towards Tuas after Eunos Link exit, which is the corridor the optimal route uses, and its 20:02-21:35 window overlaps the trip; the route left that corridor before the affected segment and rejoined it. The driver was right to avoid the accident and is not fined for it. But the exoneration is capped: justified excess = min(7.07, 1.30 x (30.1 - 27.1) + 1.00) = 4.90 km. The driver's own trace, 34.17 km, is 4.07 km longer than the 30.1 km shortest lawful alternative the advisory made available; that mileage is the driver's choice, not the accident's. The second advisory (ADV-20260716-055, CTE towards SLE, intersects_route false) exonerates nothing: it covers a corridor the optimal route never uses.

THE REFUND. The closure-adjusted optimal is 27.1 + 4.90 = 32.00 km, with duration scaled from the booked 34.0 to 40.1 minutes. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 32.00 + 0.28 x 40.1) x 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 39.828. Refund = 43.41 charged_total - 39.828 = 3.582, rounded up to SGD 3.60. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the fare, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. Charged_total 43.41, recomputed_fare 39.828 and refund 3.60 are the three lines.

ON THE DRIVER'S "NO ACTION" ARGUMENT. I do not accept that the 2.17 km residue fails POL-RD-01 and leaves the whole charge standing. POL-RD-03 states expressly that excess beyond the cap is not exonerated and IS refunded under POL-RD-02 computed against the closure-adjusted optimal route, and POL-RD-02 directs its computation onto the adjusted route wherever POL-RD-03 excuses part of the excess. The 2.17 km is the part no closure explains, and it is refunded. The driver's fallback figure of a 3.60 ceiling is therefore right; his primary request that nothing be refunded is not.

ON THE RIDER'S ALTERNATIVE FIGURE. The SGD 9.00 computed on the unadjusted 27.1 km / 34.0 min baseline is not available: the POL-RD-03 exoneration is made out on the cited advisory, its window and the route geometry, so the refund runs on the adjusted baseline, not the booked one. The rider's sense that 43.41 is about 14.00 more than usual is not the measure the policy uses.

OTHER CLAUSES. POL-RD-04 does not apply: the reroute was the driver's own proposal ('accident on PIE after eunos, i go ECP instead ok'); the rider's 'ok but not too long ah' is not an instruction naming a road or place, and waypoint_hint is null, so no rider-requested detour is made out and no excess is excluded on that ground. POL-RD-05 does not open (no amended pickup or dropoff, no amended optimal stored). POL-RD-11 does not apply: the fare model is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null, so the distance-and-time refund route is not closed. POL-RD-09 adds nothing: erp_gantries is empty, the off-route ERP total is 0.00, and there is no airport surcharge, so there is no pass-through correction and no billing-integrity referral. POL-RD-08 is satisfied on both sides as described, and the rider's profile does not trigger the extra-corroboration rule. The charge is live (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued 0.00).

Both parties' profiles were used only to weight credibility; no context-only field (ratings, acceptance rate, account age, lifetime counters, prior disputes) has been used to decide anything about this trip.

No mandatory escalation applies: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the trip identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, no timestamps conflict, no exculpatory clause was invoked against a missing or inapplicable artifact, and the refund is well within the POL-RD-10(6) ceiling. Confidence 0.9, the cap being the full weight of the artifacts that carry the deciding facts.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and to the driver: this is a route-deviation case on the Toa Payoh Central to Bugis Junction trip of 17 July 2026 (TRP-00106).

Finding on the route. The governing GPS trace (EV-GPS-00106) measures 10.78 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff against a booked optimal of 7.2 km (EV-TRIP-00106). POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern, and it forbids citing the trip record's rounded 10.8 km convenience copy for the threshold test; measured the way the clause requires, the excess is 3.58 km, or 49.72% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km absolute), so the deviation is ESTABLISHED. The same figure sits just below the 50%-of-optimal and 8.0 km lines that would make the deviation additionally MATERIAL, so no material-deviation finding is recorded. I do not treat the trace as impaired: it carries 169 fixes at a 10-second interval with 100% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, nowhere near the POL-RD-07 thresholds. Both advocates' readings of this arithmetic are accepted.

No exoneration. Nothing excuses the excess. There is no traffic advisory that can exonerate under POL-RD-03: EV-ADVIS-00106-01 is present but empty, so it names no road and asserts no closure, and its absence is itself citable. The single in-app message (EV-CHAT-00106, sent 08:46:30) is a complaint, not an instruction; it carries no waypoint hint and names no road, so the POL-RD-04 corroboration test cannot be run, the clause is unavailable, and no distance is excluded from excess. There was no amended pickup or dropoff (POL-RD-05 is not engaged) and this is not a pooled trip (POL-RD-12 is not engaged; vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI).

Refund. The fare is METERED and no exoneration applies, so POL-RD-02 fixes the outcome arithmetically, not by discretion: charged_total is 26.04; the recomputed optimal-route fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 7.2 + 0.28 x 19.0) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP on the optimal route + no fixed surcharge, no waiting fee, no promo = 15.32. The refund is 26.04 - 15.32 = 10.72, rounded up to SGD 10.75. That is 41.2% of the charged total, well under the 90% that would make it a FULL_REFUND, and well above the 0.50 de minimis floor, so it is a PARTIAL_REFUND.

ERP. The 5.50 of ERP (3.00 at CTE Braddell Rd and 2.50 at the CTE Chin Swee tunnel, both off the optimal route) is already comprehended inside the 10.75, because the recomputed fare credits only gantries lying on the optimal route and the optimal route carries none. It is itemised here for transparency and must not be added on top, per POL-RD-09(1). Both gantries are matched to the trace (nearest fixes 0.0 m and 24.1 m, inside the 250 m radius) and airport_surcharge is 0.0 on a non-airport trip, so no separate billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) arises.

Driver compensation. There is no unbilled-distance shortfall: the fare_breakdown charged 10.8 km against a 10.78 km trace, so POL-RD-04's compensation limb is not triggered and no payment to the driver is due.

Escalation and referrals. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing or non-covering artifact; the refund is far below the 150.00 ceiling; and every charge line has a counterpart. No POL-RD-06 repeat pattern exists (0 deviation flags across 96 completed trips), so there is no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral. No POL-RD-09(4) referral arises. The referrals list is therefore empty.

Outcome. The rider's claim of a genuine detour is supported, but the contest is a partial one: SGD 10.75 of the 26.04 charged is returned to the rider as a PARTIAL_REFUND.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Rider and driver, this is what the record supports.

DEVIATION. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is the GPS trace: 54.16 km on EV-GPS-00105 against the booked optimal of 36.0 km on EV-TRIP-00105 — an excess of 18.16 km, 50.4% of optimal. That clears both establishment gates (20% and 0.8 km) and both materiality gates (50% and 8.0 km), so this is an established AND material deviation. The rounded trip_record figure of 54.2 km was not used for the threshold test.

THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXPLANATION. The driver says heavy PIE traffic made him take another way. That is an assertion citing no evidence ID, and POL-RD-08 disposes of it: it is discarded and does not shift the burden. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00105-01, has a null payload (weight 0.0): it names no road, carries no validity window and no shortest-lawful-alternative distance, so the POL-RD-03 exoneration test cannot be run and no part of the excess is excused. Because the driver never invoked POL-RD-03 against any artifact — his statement cites neither an artifact nor a clause — this is not the POL-RD-10(5) situation of a clause invoked against a cited but deficient artifact, and it does not convert a decidable case into an escalation. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: trip IDs match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired (empty gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0); timestamps line up with nothing running backwards; the refund is below both SGD 150.00 and charged_total; and every charge line has a counterpart.

REFUND. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs: recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 36.0 + 0.28 x 42.0) x 1.0 (the surge multiplier read from EV-FARE-00105) + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 surcharge - 0 promo = SGD 43.36, giving charged_total 65.13 - 43.36 = SGD 21.77, rounded up to SGD 21.80. That is the POL-RD-02 figure, and it is 33.4% of the charge.

UPLIFT. POL-RD-06 is engaged because the deviation is MATERIAL. On EV-DPROF-00105, deviation_flags_90d is 4, which meets the '3 or more' limb. The repeat-deviation pattern is therefore ESTABLISHED, and because this trip's deviation is material and substantiated on its own trace, POL-RD-06(b) licenses FULL_REFUND of charged_total in place of the POL-RD-02 partial. The two figures sit side by side as the clause requires: POL-RD-02 partial SGD 21.80, uplifted figure SGD 65.13. No pass-through lines are carved out — ERP is 0.00, tolls 0.00 and airport_surcharge 0.00, correctly so because this trip ENDS at Changi and does not originate there. The rider's demand for the entire fare is granted, on POL-RD-06(b) and not on the 90%-of-charge limb of POL-RD-02.

PROFILE FIELDS. Only deviation_flags_90d and completed_trips_90d were used, and only for the POL-RD-06 test that names them. The driver's rating 4.31, acceptance_rate 0.94, prior_disputes_filed 5 and prior_deviation_flags 6 are context only under POL-GEN-01 and carried no weight; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags was not substituted for the trailing-90-day figure.

OTHER DEFENCES. No rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04: the chat log contains only the rider's questions, no instruction and no waypoint_hint, so nothing is excluded from excess. No relocation under POL-RD-05: both amendment timestamps and both amended fields are null. No pooling under POL-RD-12: vehicle_type is RYDE_X, so the baseline is the ordinary 36.0 km optimal. Nothing is added on top of the refund under POL-RD-09.

CONDUCT REFERRAL. POL-RD-06(c) adds a referral to driver-conduct review; it rides with the refund and does not delay or displace it. One open item for a human reviewer, recorded here rather than as a referral: the bundle contains no usable LTA traffic advisory for the PIE corridor on 2026-07-15 between 14:33 and 15:44. That is a data-quality gap, not a reason to hold this ruling.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — this dispute turns on which route the trip is measured against, and the record answers it.

WHAT WAS DRIVEN. Under POL-RD-01 the governing measurement is the GPS polyline, not the receipt: the trace records 26.17 km. The 26.2 km on the fare record is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not used for the threshold test. The trace is clean — 100% coverage, 206 fixes, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0, a steady 10-second sampling interval — so it is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) and the reading stands.

WHICH BASELINE APPLIES. You moved the pickup to Punggol MRT in the chat at 07:11:58, which the platform recorded as pickup_amended_at 07:12:30, and you then asked to change the destination from Terminal 1 to Terminal 3 at 07:41:40, recorded as dropoff_amended_at 07:41:52, to which the driver agreed. Because both endpoints were amended after booking, POL-RD-05 requires POL-RD-01 to be re-run against the optimal route between the AMENDED endpoints. The platform's stored re-quote for that route is amended_optimal_distance_km 24.6 km, with a duration of 31.0 minutes. The 21.0 km figure on your receipt is the booked Rivervale Drive–to–Terminal 1 route, which was never driven after your changes; it is the wrong comparator and I cannot use it.

THE THRESHOLD. The excess over the amended optimal is 26.17 − 24.6 = 1.57 km, which is 6.4% of 24.6 km. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH that the excess exceed 20% of optimal AND that it exceed 0.8 km. The 1.57 km passes the absolute limb but the 6.4% fails the percentage limb, so no deviation is ESTABLISHED. POL-RD-01 states that where either establishment test fails, no deviation exists and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The driver's advocate's first, second, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh and eighth claims are accepted in this respect; the rider's advocate's second claim (trace governs at 26.17 km) is accepted, and its third and fourth claims (deviation on the booked baseline) are rejected for the reason just given.

THE AIRPORT CIRCLING. The driver's own statement concedes he went round the T3 loop twice looking for you, and I treat that admission as evidence against his interest. It does not change the outcome. The distance he covered doing so is already inside the measured excess, and even counting it in full the excess stays far below the 20% limb. In any event POL-RD-05 excludes circling within 400 m of the amended point for more than 4 minutes, and the rider's advocate's fifth claim correctly notes that the arrival block is unavailable because trip_record.pickup_zone_class is null so no zone was substituted — but that fact, whichever way it cuts, cannot lift a 6.4% excess over a 20% threshold.

EXCULPATORY CLAUSES. The rider's advocate's sixth claim is accepted: POL-RD-03 can exonerate nothing because the only traffic advisory on file (EV-ADVIS-00108-01) carries a null payload and names no road, and POL-RD-04 cannot be run as a rider-requested detour because every chat message carries a null waypoint_hint and names no road. Neither clause is needed, because no deviation was established in the first place.

PASS-THROUGH AND BILLING. The rider's advocate's seventh claim at POL-RD-09 is accepted: erp_gantries is empty, tolls/ERP are 0.00, and the airport surcharge is 0.00, which is correct for a trip that ENDS at Changi. There is no unmatched charge line and no billing-integrity correction. No referral arises under POL-RD-09(4).

REMEDY. Because no deviation survives, the POL-RD-02 recomputation is never reached and the rider's advocate's eighth claim (recomputed fare 27.63, refund 6.14 → 6.15) does not apply. The charged total of $33.77 stands.

PROFILES. The rider's advocate's ninth claim is accepted. Under POL-RD-06 the driver's deviation_flags_90d is 0 against 402 completed trips over 90 days, below both limbs (3 or more flags; ratio 0.05 with at least 40 trips), so no repeat pattern is established and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral issues. Under POL-RD-08 the rider's deviation_claims_60d of 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 0 are below the 4 and 1 thresholds, so no extra corroboration is required. Every other field on both profiles (rating, account age, lifetime trips, cancellation rate, prior counters) is context only under POL-GEN-01 and grounds no finding; the referee flagged the mention of 'rating' in the rider's claim as context-only, and it was used correctly there, so nothing is discarded.

CONFIDENCE AND ESCALATION. The deciding facts — the amended optimal distance (EV-TRIP-00108) and the trace distance (EV-GPS-00108) — are carried by two independent, unimpaired artifacts, both at full weight, and the amendment facts are independently corroborated by the chat log (EV-CHAT-00108), which is a contemporaneous record made from inside the disputed window. Confidence is therefore well above the 0.70 floor set by POL-GEN-02 and POL-RD-10(1). No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: trip identifiers match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown; the trace is unimpaired; timestamps agree and run forwards; no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact; no refund figure exceeds any cap; and no charge line is unmatched.

OUTCOME. The rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present state stands: the $33.77 charge is neither collected nor refunded again — payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays 0.00. This is NO_ACTION under POL-GEN-03. If you believe the driver's circling exceeded what the platform's re-quote allowed for, the open point for review is whether the re-quoted amended optimal properly accounted for the T3 loop; that is a question for a reviewer, and it is not a clause-mandated referral, so it is recorded here rather than in the referrals list.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both of you.

WHAT HAPPENED, IN FIGURES. The trip was charged 37.74 SGD (fare_breakdown charged_total). It ran 29.98 km on the GPS trace (trace_distance_km), which governs over the rounded 30.0 km convenience copy on the trip record. Against the 24.0 km booked optimal, the excess is 5.98 km, i.e. 24.92%. That passes the POL-RD-01 establishment gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation IS established. It does not reach the materiality gates (8.0 km / 50%), so it is not a MATERIAL deviation and no POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern check, uplift or conduct referral arises.

WHY NOTHING IS REFUNDED. The deviation is fully exonerated under POL-RD-03. The LTA advisory ADV-20260803-014 records a HIGH-severity all-lanes closure on the PIE towards Tuas after Clementi Rd, 07:10 to 09:30. On the computed facts it intersects the booked optimal corridor (intersects_route = true) and it overlaps the trip window (07:47:40 to 08:25:40). The actual route left the optimal corridor before the affected segment and rejoined after it: both accounts agree on the same diversion (off at Bukit Panjang, Upper Bukit Timah, the AYE), the advisory itself prescribes exactly that diversion, and the driver told the rider so in the chat at 07:54:20, inside the trip window, with the rider reading and answering it. The exoneration cap is the lesser of the measured 5.98 km and 1.30 x (29.2 km shortest lawful alternative - 24.0 km booked optimal) + 1.00 km tolerance = 7.76 km. The lesser figure is 5.98 km, so the whole measured excess is justified.

POL-RD-02 then runs against the closure-adjusted optimal (24.0 + 5.98 = 29.98 km; 37.5 minutes, the 30.0-minute booked duration scaled by 29.98/24.0). This is set out on separate lines as the clause requires: charged_total 37.74; recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 29.98 + 0.28 x 37.5) x 1.0 (surge read from fare_breakdown) + 0.80 platform fee = 37.585; refund = 37.74 - 37.585 = 0.155 SGD. That is below the 0.50 SGD de minimis, so no refund issues. The fare breakdown carries no gantry lines at all (ERP totals 0.00, on and off optimal route), so the POL-RD-09(2) pass-through correction available on a closure exoneration comes to nothing, and no other pass-through or billing-integrity line exists.

THE RIDER'S POINTS. The threshold showing under POL-RD-08 is accepted: the same trip TRP-00111 appears on the trip record, trace and fare breakdown, and the excess of 5.98 km measured from an unimpaired trace meets POL-RD-01. A rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 is correctly not available: the only rider message is 'as long as i reach by 8.30', which names no place or road, and both chat messages carry waypoint_hint null, so the clause is unavailable and the case is decided on the remaining clauses. The suggestion that the routing engine's 07:44 snapshot, which still returned BKE southbound then PIE westbound, contradicts the advisory is rejected: the booked optimal is the baseline POL-RD-01 fixes, the intersection of the advisory with that corridor is a computed fact this tribunal does not re-derive, and the clause notes expressly forbid reading a substitute optimal out of the free text of optimal_route_source. It does not create a POL-RD-10(7) contradiction, because the rider opposes the advisory with no admissible artifact of comparable strength - 'I did not see any closure' cites no evidence and carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The rider's alternative arithmetic (37.74 - 31.00 = 6.74, rounded 6.75) is the correct figure ONLY if the closure did not apply; because it does apply, that figure is superseded. On the profile points both sides are right: POL-GEN-01 confines the profiles to the tests that name their fields, nothing on either profile is used against anyone, and the driver's lifetime counters are context only.

No mandatory escalation trigger in POL-RD-10 fires: identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 229 fixes, 10-second interval, no gaps), timestamps run forward and consistently, the exculpatory clause is invoked on an artifact that exists, covers the window and carries every field it needs, the residual refund is nowhere near 150.00 SGD, no charge line is unmatched and no two sides rest on mutually contradictory admissible evidence. Because this is a rider-filed dispute, NO_ACTION leaves the existing charge and payment status as they stand; the disputed 8.00 SGD is not refunded and no compensation is payable to the driver. One open observation for the record, which does not change the outcome: the routing-engine wording on the trip record is not used to build the optimal, and a customer-facing note could explain to riders why a genuinely closed expressway can still lengthen a billed trip while leaving no refund due.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: I accept that you were charged SGD 26.83 and that your own Punggol-to-Raffles-Place route is about 15.8 km. But this was a RYDE_POOL booking. Under POL-RD-12, the baseline for a pooled trip is the platform’s matched pooled itinerary, stored on the trip_record as optimal_distance_km = 19.4 km, not the solo-rider figure solo_optimal_distance_km = 15.8 km, which is reference only. The app told you at 18:42:04, before the trip started, that a co-rider at Hougang had been matched and that the pooled route was estimated at 19.4 km. The Hougang leg is therefore the co-rider pickup, not an unexplained driver detour. The governing GPS trace distance is 20.18 km, an excess of 0.78 km over 19.4 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be both greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%. It is neither. Even using the rounded trip_record distance of 20.2 km, the excess is exactly 0.80 km, which is still not greater than 0.8 km, and 4.1%, far below 20%. Addressed to both of you.

To both parties. This trip deviated, and the refund is the arithmetic one.

THE DEVIATION. POL-RD-01 measures the excess on gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which is 23.97 km, against the booked optimal of 18.0 km — an excess of 5.97 km, or 33.2%. The 24.0 km on the trip record is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and is not the figure the threshold test uses. Both establishment gates are passed (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so the deviation is established. The excess reaches neither materiality gate (50% or 8.0 km), so this is not a MATERIAL deviation and POL-RD-06 is not engaged: there is no repeat-deviation uplift and no driver-conduct referral. The rider's profile does not change this either — deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4, so no corroboration beyond the trace is required. The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 (241 fixes at a 10 s interval, 100% coverage, no gap over 90 s, no jump over 500 m), so the deviation needs no corroboration; in any event the fare ledger's off-optimal Adam Road gantry independently places the vehicle off the optimal corridor, and the driver's chat message — 'AYE jam boss, this way faster' — admits the reroute.

NO EXCUSE RUNS. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction and the only rider message is a complaint about the route, not a request; waypoint_hint is null, so that test cannot be run. POL-RD-05 and POL-RD-12 do not apply (no endpoint was amended; the vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL). POL-RD-03 requires a traffic advisory and there is none. The driver's account that the AYE was crawling is a general assertion that traffic was bad, and POL-RD-08 is explicit that such an assertion, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's burden. I do NOT escalate on the empty advisory (EV-ADVIS-00114-01, no payload, weight 0.0). POL-RD-10(5) fires where an exculpatory clause is invoked against a CITED artifact that is missing; here the driver cites no evidence at all and his own statement records 'No advisory that I know of.' The advisory's absence is itself citable and defeats the excuse on the merits; it is not a gap that stops the case being decided on a complete, unimpaired trace.

THE MONEY. The fare is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 18.0 + 0.28 x 30.0) x 1.6) + 0.80 platform fee + 2.50 on-route ERP = 44.42. The 1.6 multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier and is preserved on the optimal route — the rider accepts the surge and the recomputation charges it. charged_total is 58.10. The refund is 58.10 - 44.42 = 13.68, rounded UP to SGD 13.70. That is 23.6% of the charge, well short of the 90% that would convert it to a full refund and well above the 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The $2.00 Adam Road ERP line is itemised for transparency but is already comprehended in that figure and is never added on top (POL-RD-09(1)); both charged gantries are matched to the trace within the 250 m radius (0.0 m and 8.76 m), so neither is a phantom line and no billing-integrity referral arises. No driver compensation is due: the distance billed (24.0 km) is not short of the trace.

In short: the rider's 'extra 6 km' is 5.97 km on the measurement the clause governs, and the recoverable sum is SGD 13.70 — not the 15.00 contested, and not the 15.70 that would double-count the off-route ERP.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).

To both parties. The disputed trip TRP-00115 ran on 8 Aug 2026 from Marina Bay Financial Centre to Woodlands, and the money question turns on how it was priced, not on how it was driven. EV-FARE-00115 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 34.50 and total_charged 39.00. The driver's explanation that 'CTE was heavy' is a bare assertion with no advisory behind it and carries no weight; the rider's one-word 'ok' to the driver's reroute message does not make the detour rider-requested under POL-RD-04, because the rider named no road or waypoint (waypoint_hint is null on both messages), so POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record. The same 2.00 is a phantom charge refundable in full under POL-RD-09(4); it is refunded once and not added twice. The refund of 2.00 is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of charged_total, so this is a PARTIAL_REFUND, not NO_ACTION and not FULL_REFUND. The billing-integrity finding above is recorded as a referral under POL-RD-09(4); it rides with the money and does not hold it back. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires: identifiers match across the three artifacts, the trace is unimpaired (100% coverage, 229 fixes at a 10 s interval, no gaps), no timestamps run backwards, and the only unmatched charge line is the AYE line, which POL-RD-10(8) expressly excludes because POL-RD-09(4) refunds it. No artifact below weight 1.0 carries the deciding facts (the trace and fare breakdown are clean), so the confidence floor is met.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged for trip TRP-00201 is refunded to you in full. Driver — you receive no compensation, because the no-show fee was never chargeable.

What decides the case is the GPS trace. A no-show fee stands only if all four conditions in POL-NS-01 hold. Two do: the trip record contains an 'arrived' event for this trip (08:02:14), and the driver terminated it at 08:09:40 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event. The other two do not. The trace records 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes and the driver's closest recorded approach to the Blk 118 Rivervale Dr pin was 779.93 m (mean 1,177.11 m), against a STANDARD arrival radius of 50 m — so limb (b) fails. The effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 s against the 300 s minimum, a shortfall of 300 s — so limb (c) fails too. The trip record's own 7.4-minute clock does not save the fee: that clock runs from the 08:02:14 arrival marker, and at that moment the trace puts the driver more than 779 m from the pin, past the 300 m line in POL-NS-05. The marker is therefore FALSE, it never started the waiting clock, and the clock recomputed from the first qualifying in-geofence fix is zero. Because there is no qualifying in-geofence fix anywhere in the trip, POL-NS-05(ii) refunds the fee in full, pays the driver nothing, and records a false-arrival event against him — that is the referral below.

POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 reach the same result independently: no qualifying in-radius fix in the 15 minutes before cancellation, and a 300 s dwell shortfall. POL-NS-06(i) cannot accumulate any dwell because the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00201-01 is MISSING (no payload, weight 0.0); it carries no fact and is citable only for its absence, so it neither exonerates the driver nor triggers escalation.

The rider is also exonerated under POL-NS-04: her message at 08:05:33, 'hello? i dont see any car at 118', falls inside the waiting window; the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor made any in-app call before cancelling; and her device stayed within 24.92 m of the pin across all 122 qualifying fixes, well inside the 100 m STANDARD presence radius.

POL-NS-03 does not apply: the 400 m wrong-entrance ceiling is exceeded, and registered_pickup_points is 1, so no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises. POL-NS-07 pays the driver nothing because POL-NS-01 is not satisfied in full; the anti-farming check it names does not trip either (no_show_terminations_30d = 3, below 4, and 3 / 96 = 0.031, below 0.08), and no adverse finding rests on any context-only profile field.

No escalation: the trip record's arrival marker and the trace conflict on arrival, but POL-NS-05 is the clause that resolves precisely that conflict by declaring the marker false; no artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) (10 s fix cadence, no gaps, 2 chat messages matching the trip record, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation line equals the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee of 4.00 and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee of 4.00); and the remaining POL-NS-09 limbs are clear. Confidence is 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. Figures used: cancellation_fee SGD 4.00 (fare breakdown EV-FARE-00201), refund SGD 4.00, driver compensation SGD 0.00.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the SGD 6.00 no-show fee on trip TRP-00202 stands, and the driver is owed SGD 4.80. Here is how I got there.

THE FEE IS CHARGEABLE UNDER POL-NS-01. All four limbs hold on the code-computed facts, and the rider's own advocate conceded each of them rather than pretending otherwise:
(a) EV-TRIP-00202 records the driver's 'arrived' event at 2026-07-24T23:13:10.
(b) EV-GPS-00202 places the driver inside the 150 m AIRPORT arrival radius from 23:12:45 — 25 seconds before that event — with 63 qualifying in-radius fixes and a closest approach of about 22 m. The POL-NS-02 proximity test is met on admissible fixes, and the AIRPORT zone class comes from trip_record, not from assumption.
(c) The driver's single continuous in-geofence run ran 620 seconds, from 23:12:45 to 23:23:05, measured from the first qualifying fix as POL-NS-01(c) requires (not from the arrived tap). That is 140 seconds more than the 480-second minimum for AIRPORT.
(d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 23:23:20, after the minimum dwell elapsed at 23:20:45, on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, with no boarding event anywhere in the record.

NO RIDER ROUTE DISPLACES THE FEE. POL-NS-05 (false arrival marker) does not fire: at the 23:13:10 marker the driver was already stationary inside the geofence, roughly 22 m from the pin — neither more than 300 m away nor travelling at 15 km/h or above. POL-NS-06 (waiting-period shortfall) has nothing to bite on: there is no shortfall. POL-NS-04 (rider contact unanswered by driver) is closed at its own threshold — limb (a) requires at least one locating or coordinating message sent BY THE RIDER during the waiting window, and EV-CHAT-00202 holds only the SYSTEM arrival notice and two driver messages; there is no rider message and no in-app call in trip_record.in_app_calls. POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance) does not apply, because the driver's qualifying fixes fall inside the arrival radius rather than outside it but within 400 m.

THE RIDER'S REQUEST TO WAIVE THE CHARGE IS NOT SUPPORTED. The rider asks that the charge be excused because his flight was delayed and he did not see the messages until later. His account is consistent with the unread (read_at null) timestamps on the driver's messages, and I do not doubt he was delayed — but no clause makes the fee turn on that. POL-NS-06 fixes the fee against the driver's dwell 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', and POL-NS-01 contains no rider-presence limb at all. The rider was right to say his whereabouts are not an element of the charge; that cuts against him here, because his absence from the pin does not defeat the fee either.

THE AMOUNT. The SGD 6.00 charged reconciles with fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the GREATER of the AIRPORT zone-class fee (SGD 6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) is SGD 6.00, exactly the fare_breakdown cancellation-fee line. There is no fare defect under POL-NS-08(d).

DRIVER COMPENSATION UNDER POL-NS-07. Because POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it, the driver is compensated at 80 percent of SGD 6.00 = SGD 4.80. The anti-farming guard does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (the threshold is 4), and 1 of 168 completed trips in 30 days is far below the 0.08 rate. Neither limb is met, so compensation is paid. Per POL-GEN-03, a DRIVER_COMPENSATION ruling carries the same figure in amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd; the rider's own charge is unaffected and remains SGD 6.00.

PROFILE FIELDS. The rider's advocate is correct that prior_no_show_flags, prior_disputes_filed, prior_disputes_upheld, rating, lifetime_trips and acceptance_rate are context only under POL-GEN-01 and ground no finding either way; only the POL-NS-07 counters (no_show_terminations_30d, completed_trips_30d) are citable, and they clear the driver. The referee's flags on these mentions are warnings, not discards.

MISSING TRAFFIC ADVISORY. EV-ADVIS-00202-01 is MISSING and carries no weight (weight 0.0, POL-GEN-02). It is not needed for this outcome: the dwell is a single 620-second interval, so POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is never invoked.

CONFIDENCE AND REFERRALS. The deciding facts rest on EV-GPS-00202, EV-TRIP-00202 and EV-FARE-00202; no impairment was disclosed against any of them, and the escalating conditions of POL-NS-09 do not arise — the driver arrival and dwell facts are uncontradicted, the anti-farming check is clear, and the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (the POL-NS-09(d) threshold is 3). No clause produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

This dispute is about the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-00203. EV-FARE-00203 shows cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00.

Both sides accept the driver reached the pickup. EV-TRIP-00203 records an 'arrived' event at 19:41:35, and EV-GPS-00203 holds 21 qualifying fixes inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, the closest 18.7 m from the pin. So POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) and the POL-NS-02 proximity test are satisfied, and no false-arrival case arises under POL-NS-05 (the driver was stationary well within 300 m at the marker, so there is no false-arrival referral against him).

The fee nonetheless fails POL-NS-01 limb (c). That limb measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from the 'arrived' tap. The trace's only in-geofence run starts at 19:41:20 and ends at 19:44:35 — 195 seconds — against the 300-second STANDARD minimum. That is a shortfall of 105 seconds. Limb (d) fails for the same reason: the required 300 seconds would have run out at about 19:46:20, but the driver terminated at 19:44:40 (EV-TRIP-00203 gives arrived 19:41:35, cancelled 19:44:40, wait_time_min 3.1).

POL-NS-06 fixes the consequence: where the effective dwell is shorter than the minimum, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she responded to messages. The one route to a longer dwell — accumulating separate in-geofence intervals under POL-NS-06(i) — is closed twice over: there is only one in-geofence interval (run_count 1), and the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00203-01 is MISSING (payload null, weight 0.0), so the limb cannot be run and nothing may be added to the 195 seconds. POL-NS-03 does not apply either: the driver was inside the arrival radius, not at the wrong face of the venue.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate anyone, and both sides accept this: the driver replied at 19:44:31, 101 seconds after the rider's 19:42:50 message, inside the 120-second window. It changes nothing, because the refund flows from the dwell shortfall and does not depend on the rider's presence or response. The RIDER_NO_SHOW reason code likewise does not match what the chat log shows — the rider was actively coordinating and the driver cancelled before the paid five minutes had run.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and POL-NS-06 says that where the dwell still falls short the full refund stands and no compensation is payable. The SGD 3.20 figure in the fare breakdown's derived block is therefore not funded from the SGD 4.00 the rider was charged.

No escalation ground is engaged. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (driver no_show_terminations_30d 2 is below 4, and 2/131 is below 0.08); both parties' counterparty-dispute counts are 0, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged. No artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08: there is no clock skew (arrived 19:41:35, cancelled and last fix 19:44:40), no sampling gap (max_gap_sec 0.0, 60 fixes), the chat's 3 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count 3, and the SGD 4.00 cancellation-fee line reconciles with the fee schedule (STANDARD 4.00 vs RYDE_X 4.00, greater 4.00). The only sub-1.0 artifact is the MISSING advisory at weight 0.0, which carries nothing and on which this refund does not rest; the deciding fact rests on EV-GPS-00203 and EV-TRIP-00203.

Outcome: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded in full to the rider. Nothing further is ordered. The waiting-period shortfall, not any finding against the driver, drives this result — the driver is not penalised beyond losing the fee.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee charged on 26 July 2026 does not stand. It is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Driver, your baseline case is made out on the platform's own telemetry, and I accept it. No POL-NS-09 trigger is engaged — confidence is above the 0.70 floor, neither party has any trailing no-show disputes with the other, the rider has no no-show disputes in 30 days, and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip. EV-ADVIS-00204-01 is a MISSING traffic advisory (weight 0.0), but nothing in this ruling rests on it: with a single in-geofence interval, POL-NS-06 limb (i) accumulation is unavailable in any event, so its absence changes nothing. For completeness, the rider's filed narrative refers to 'Entrance 1' while the message on file and the registered pickup point both say Entrance 3; that discrepancy decides no limb, since the geofence tests are met on distance and the rider's device sits within 40 m of the pin.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both of you are answered here. The $4.00 cancellation fee cannot stand, and it is refunded to the rider in full.

Why the charge fails. A no-show fee is chargeable only if all four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold, and three of them fail on this record. Limb (b): the GPS trace carries 92 driver fixes across the whole pickup attempt (07:18:05 to 07:33:05) and not one falls inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius around the pin at Blk 118 — derived.arrival.qualifying_fix_count is 0, the longest qualifying in-geofence run is 0.0 seconds, and the driver's closest approach at any moment was 259.94 m. Limb (c): the in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum (POL-NS-06), a shortfall of 300 seconds, and limb (c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence fix — not from the 'arrived' marker at 07:26:40, and not from the trip record's wait_time_min of 6.4. Limb (d): the trip was terminated with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which POL-NS-01 expressly excludes and describes as the driver's own admission that he could not find the rider. The driver advocate concedes all of this, and I accept it.

What this was. A wrong-face arrival. The driver's closest point, 259.94 m from the pin, is outside the 50 m arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, so POL-NS-03 governs and the fee is refunded in full. On fault, POL-NS-03(i) applies: the rider stated her block in the chat ('im at blk 118, the one facing the carpark', 07:22:10) and the driver answered 'ok coming' at 07:22:48 but never moved to it before cancelling at 07:33:05, so the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation. POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is unavailable: it needs trip_record.registered_pickup_points of 2 or more, and the figure here is 1.

The driver's money. No compensation is payable under POL-NS-07. That clause pays 80 percent of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. The anti-farming check is not reached, and does not trip in any event: 2 no-show terminations against 104 completed trips in 30 days is a rate of about 0.019, below the 0.08 rate and below the count of 4, and the lifetime counter prior_no_show_flags is not the field that clause reads. The driver advocate does not press compensation, and I accept that.

Why this is not escalated. I reject the driver advocate's submission that the case must be held and escalated under POL-NS-09(b). That trigger needs two admissible artifacts to contradict each other directly on arrival, dwell or rider presence and no clause to resolve the conflict. POL-NS-03 resolves this one: a driver who waits at the wrong face within 400 m of the pin, as this one did at 259.94 m, produces a full refund with no compensation, and on either reading — POL-NS-02 or POL-NS-03 — the rider wins. No other POL-NS-09 trigger fires: rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (below 3), both parties' disputes_with_counterparty_90d are 0, and nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08 — the trace has 92 fixes with max_gap_sec 0.0 and 100 percent coverage, the chat log's 4 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 4 with no gap over 5 minutes, the arrival marker is within 10 seconds of the surrounding fixes (well inside the 90-second skew tolerance), and the fare line reconciles with fee_schedule (the greater of the STANDARD zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee, both SGD 4.00). So I rule money rather than hold the fee.

Other points. POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied to the rider's locating message 38 seconds later, inside the 120-second window, so limb (b) fails and the clause is unavailable — both sides agree, and it changes nothing. No false-arrival referral is made under POL-NS-05: that clause catches a driver marking arrival more than 300 m from the pin or while travelling at 15 km/h or above, and the driver's closest approach over the entire trace is 259.94 m, inside that band, so no false-arrival event is recorded against him.

The money. The fare breakdown shows one charge only: a SGD 4.00 cancellation fee, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, with no booking or platform fee line. The full contested amount, SGD 4.00, is refunded to the rider, and no driver compensation is payable. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00205-01) is MISSING with weight 0.0; POL-NS-06(i) is therefore unavailable, but that costs nothing here because there are zero in-geofence intervals to sum. Confidence is 0.90: the deciding facts — no in-geofence arrival and the termination code — are carried at full weight by the GPS trace and the trip record, and the absent advisory carries no fact in this ruling.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

Both sides have argued this on the same facts and, unusually, they now agree on the arithmetic. The driver's arrival case under POL-NS-01 is made out on all four limbs: (a) EV-TRIP-00207 records the 'arrived' event at 06:41:20 on 29 July 2026; (b) EV-GPS-00207 places the driver inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 06:41:10 — closest fix 14.47 m from the Blk 682 Woodlands Ave 6 pin, 52 admissible in-radius fixes, 100% coverage and no sampling gap — so the POL-NS-02 proximity test is satisfied; (c) he then held position continuously for 507 seconds against the 300-second STANDARD minimum, a 207-second surplus, so POL-NS-06 is not reached and no full refund issues on a shortfall ground; and (d) the trip was terminated by the driver at 06:49:37 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the required dwell had elapsed, with no boarding event. POL-NS-05 does not bite — at the arrival timestamp he was stationary inside the geofence, not more than 300 m out and not travelling at 15 km/h or above — and POL-NS-03 is not engaged because he held position inside the arrival radius rather than at the wrong entrance. POL-NS-04 fails at its first limb: EV-CHAT-00207 holds four messages, all from the driver or the system and none from the rider, and the rider's own device track (118 fixes, minimum 1,894.10 m from the pin, 0 qualifying fixes) fails limb (c) as well. The SGD 4.00 charge reconciles exactly with fee_schedule.resolution_rule — the STANDARD zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) tie — so there is no POL-NS-08(d) defect, and no limb of POL-NS-08(a) to (d) is engaged. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00207-01 (null payload, weight 0.0) is relied on by nobody: the driver's dwell is a single continuous in-geofence run, so the accumulation of separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is not in issue and its absence carries no adverse inference.

That would ordinarily make the SGD 4.00 fee stand and entitle the driver to SGD 3.20 (80 per cent of SGD 4.00) under POL-NS-07. It does not, because POL-NS-07's anti-farming check trips on the driver's own record: EV-DPROF-00207 shows no_show_terminations_30d of 7 (threshold 4 or more) and 7 divided by 61 completed_trips_30d = 0.115 (threshold above 0.08). Both limbs are required and both hold, so the driver's compensation is WITHHELD and the case escalates under POL-NS-09(d).

ESCALATE is terminal and replaces any money outcome. No refund issues to the rider through this pipeline and no payment is made to the driver. The disputed SGD 4.00 is held — the ledger already shows it PENDING with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — rather than collected or refunded. Per POL-NS-07 the reviewer is directed to refund the rider's cancellation fee in full; that instruction is carried in the referrals list and is not netted against anything else.

On the rider's profile, POL-GEN-01 is respected: no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the POL-NS-09(d) trigger of 3, and the lifetime prior_no_show_flags counter is not the field that limb reads and was not used. One open question is left for the reviewer rather than acted on here: the rider says he came down to the pickup, while EV-GPS-00207's rider_presence block places his device roughly 1.9 km away throughout the waiting window. That conflict does not change the escalation but the reviewer may wish to consider it.

Confidence 0.90: the facts this ruling rests on — the arrival and dwell record (EV-TRIP-00207, EV-GPS-00207) and the anti-farming profile (EV-DPROF-00207) — are carried by artifacts at full weight, so nothing caps confidence below the 0.70 platform floor and the escalation rests on the POL-NS-09(d) trigger, not on any doubt about the record.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-07: the escalation packet must direct the human reviewer to refund the rider's cancellation fee of SGD 4.00 in full; the disputed fee is held on the ledger rather than collected or refunded while that review is pending.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the platform's own records decide this, and on the main point you both agree — the $4.00 cancellation fee cannot stand.

THE FEE. The driver never reached the pickup pin. His GPS trace carries 52 fixes across the whole window and not one of them falls inside the 120 m arrival radius for a LARGE_VENUE pickup; his closest approach to the pin over the entire trace was 284.95 m. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails. Limb (d) fails independently: the trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code DRIVER_UNABLE_TO_LOCATE, which is not one of the three codes limb (d) accepts (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT), and POL-NS-01 itself sends such a trip to POL-NS-03. With two limbs broken, the baseline chargeable no-show fails and the whole SGD 4.00 returns to the rider.

WHY POL-NS-03 GOVERNS, NOT POL-NS-06. [Driver] held position at the HarbourFront face of the venue: 284.95 m from the pin, outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, which the clause says is the whole test and is decidable from coordinates alone (no venue_id match is asserted — the pickup pin carries VEN-VIVOCITY and the driver's track carries none, so that corroboration is not established either way). The recorded wait of 6.6 minutes (395 seconds, against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum) and the stationary 0.0 km/h reading show a hold, not an abandonment. POL-NS-02 says in terms that where the driver was stationary for the required dwell within 400 m of the pin, POL-NS-03 governs the outcome including the driver's compensation and POL-NS-02 yields to it. I therefore reject the rider-side POL-NS-06 argument that the zero in-geofence dwell strips the driver's payment: the refund is the same full $4.00 either way, but the driver's money is fixed by POL-NS-03, not by POL-NS-06.

FAULT AND THE DRIVER'S MONEY. The chat log holds exactly two messages and both are SYSTEM ('Driver assigned. Meet at VivoCity, Lobby L.' and 'Your driver has arrived'); neither party named an entrance, block, tower or bay, and trip_record.registered_pickup_points is 4 — two or more. POL-NS-03 limb (ii) therefore applies: this was pin ambiguity, not fault on either side. That limb gives [Driver] a platform-funded goodwill payment of 50 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee = SGD 2.00, charged to the platform and never recovered from [Rider]. [Driver], your POL-NS-07 claim of SGD 3.20 is rejected: that clause compensates only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not — so your remedy is the SGD 2.00 goodwill, not SGD 3.20. Under POL-GEN-03 the rider's SGD 4.00 refund and the driver's SGD 2.00 goodwill are independent and are never netted; the ruling value (FULL_REFUND) names the filing party's outcome.

CLAIMS NOT ACCEPTED. POL-NS-05 (false arrival) is not engaged: the only distance fact on the record is the 284.95 m closest approach, inside POL-NS-05's 300 m mark, and the clause's own carve-out sends a driver stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius to POL-NS-03. No false-arrival referral is therefore produced. POL-NS-04 (rider exoneration) is not engaged either: the chat log contains no rider message, so limb (a) cannot be run — but no adverse inference about rider location is drawn, since the rider's 31 fixes sit within 22.5 m of the pin, far inside the 150 m rider-presence radius. POL-NS-07 is not reached (above). POL-NS-09 escalation is not triggered: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0 and both disputes_with_counterparty_90d fields are 0; the anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 1 against completed_trips_30d 187); and no evidence is impaired under POL-NS-08.

EVIDENCE INTEGRITY AND WEIGHT. Nothing is impaired under POL-NS-08: the trace runs the full window at 100 percent coverage, 52 driver fixes, gaps empty and max gap 0 seconds, so limb (b) is not met; the chat log's 2 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count, so limb (c) is not met; the arrival marker falls inside the trace and the trip start and termination match the first and last fixes, so limb (a) is not met; and the fare line reconciles, so limb (d) is not met — the SGD 4.00 charged is the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00). EV-ADVIS-00206-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING with weight 0.0; its absence is citable and makes POL-NS-06 limb (i) unavailable, which supports the refund rather than changing it, and no deciding fact rests on it. The deciding facts rest on the GPS trace, trip record, chat log and fare breakdown, none of which is discounted, so confidence is not capped below 1.0. Finally, POL-GEN-01: the profiles of both parties are context only and are not used as a ground of decision against either of you.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties: the SGD 8.00 no-show fee stands, and the driver is compensated SGD 6.40 of it.

WHY THE FEE STANDS (POL-NS-01). The fee is chargeable only if four conditions hold, and on this trip all four do. (a) The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-07-30T16:02:25. (b) The GPS trace's first qualifying fix inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for the pickup pin is at 16:02:10, fifteen seconds BEFORE that event, and the driver's closest approach to the pin is 28.78 m — comfortably inside (POL-NS-02; 60 qualifying in-radius fixes, well over the three required). (c) The driver then held position in one continuous in-geofence run of 585 seconds (16:02:10 to 16:11:55), clearing the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum by 285 seconds. (d) The trip record shows no boarding (started_at and ended_at are both null) and the trip was terminated by the driver at 16:12:10 on reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW, after the dwell had elapsed.

No clause displaces it. POL-NS-03 governs only a driver held stationary OUTSIDE the arrival radius; this driver was inside it, so the clause and its 400 m venue test are never reached. POL-NS-04 does not apply: the driver replied to the rider's 16:08:02 message within 18 seconds ('ok no problem', 16:08:20) and placed an answered 34-second in-app call at 16:09:40, so limb (b) fails, and limb (c) fails affirmatively — 0 of the rider's 141 fixes fall inside the 150 m rider-presence radius. POL-NS-05 is not engaged (the marker was set inside the radius, not from an expressway or arterial road), and its limb (iii) would preserve the fee anyway, since the corrected dwell still clears the minimum. POL-NS-06 has no shortfall to work on: 585 seconds against 300 seconds, a surplus of 285, not a deficit.

WHY THE RIDER'S ACCOUNT DOES NOT CHANGE THIS. The claim that the driver 'never came at all' is met by a trace putting his vehicle within about 29 m of her own pickup pin for nearly ten minutes, and by a chat log she read: the driver's 16:02:40 message naming the main guardhouse and his plate (read 16:03:01), his 16:07:15 follow-up (read 16:07:29), and her reply 'coming coming 2 min' at 16:08:02. Her 'called him also cannot get through' has nothing behind it — the only call recorded on the trip is the driver's, at 16:09:40, answered, 34 seconds. Her 'almost 15 minutes' does not match the platform's own timestamps: arrival (16:02:25) to cancellation (16:12:10) is 9 minutes 45 seconds, which matches the driver's account, not hers. On this record her own device sat stationary about 640 m from the pin from 15:54:00 to 16:15:20.

The amount is right. Under fee_schedule.resolution_rule the charge is the GREATER of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_XL vehicle-tier fee (SGD 8.00), so the vehicle-tier dimension produced the SGD 8.00; the fare line reconciles exactly (derived difference 0.00, no POL-NS-08(d) defect).

WHY THE DRIVER IS PAID. POL-NS-07 compensates at 80 percent of the itemised fee: SGD 6.40 of SGD 8.00, the residual SGD 1.60 retained as the platform service fee, matching the derived figure. The anti-farming check does not trip — it requires BOTH no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more AND a rate above 0.08; the figures are 2 and 2/143 = 0.014.

ON THE ESCALATION ARGUMENT (POL-NS-09). I have considered the submission that the chat log and the rider's GPS track conflict on rider presence and that no clause resolves it. I do not accept it. Rider presence is not a limb of the clause that decides this case — POL-NS-01 reads the driver's arrival, dwell and termination, not the rider's location — so no deciding fact is left in conflict. The clause that does read rider presence, POL-NS-04(c), is not reached because limb (b) fails, and its test would fail affirmatively in any event (0 of 141 rider fixes inside 150 m). Nor does the rider's message contradict her track: 'coming in 2 min' is consistent with a rider who never reached the pin. No POL-NS-09 trigger is open — confidence is at 0.90, above the 0.70 floor; the profile counters do not meet limbs (c) or (d) (both counterparty-dispute counters are 0, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 1); and no deciding artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a) to (d) (no clock skew beyond 90 seconds, no gap over 120 seconds and 120 fixes present, chat message count 6 matches the trip record, fare reconciles). No clause produces a referral: no false-arrival record is due under POL-NS-05(ii), and the POL-NS-07 escalation packet is not triggered.

TWO FURTHER POINTS. EV-ADVIS-00208-01 is MISSING and carries weight 0.0, so it can carry no fact; its absence neither helps nor hurts the driver — he does not need POL-NS-06(i) accumulation, because his dwell is a single continuous 585-second run. And no profile has been used to establish anything about this trip: POL-GEN-01 makes rating, lifetime trips, prior_no_show_flags and the like context only, and I have not relied on them for either party.

Outcome: the filing party's claim is not supported, the SGD 8.00 charge stands as it is, and the driver is paid SGD 6.40.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To both parties. The $6.00 no-show cancellation fee is NOT chargeable, so the state of the ledger stays exactly as it is — refund_issued_sgd 6.00, payment_status REFUNDED — and the driver's request to restore the charge is denied. Under POL-GEN-03 that disposition is NO_ACTION, which is party-relative: on a driver-filed dispute over a fee the platform has already reversed, it leaves the rider refunded. No money moves; no compensation is paid.

WHY. POL-NS-01 charges the fee only if all four conditions hold. Two are met: the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 07:38:05 (limb (a)), and the trip was terminated by the driver at 07:48:10 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW and no boarding event (limb (d)). Two fail.

(1) Limb (c), dwell. The pickup is a TRANSPORT_HUB, so the minimum continuous in-geofence dwell is 300 seconds. POL-NS-01(c) measures that dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix, not from the 'arrived' tap. The first qualifying fix is at 07:44:14 and the run ends at the 07:48:10 cancellation — 236 seconds, a 64-second shortfall (shortfall_sec 64, one qualifying run, 25 qualifying fixes against a 150 m arrival radius for a hub). The trip record's wait_time_min of 10.1 (about 605 seconds) runs from the driver's own arrival tap, and a marker the driver set does not start the clock that limb (c) defines.

(2) Limb (b). There is no qualifying in-radius fix at or before the 07:38:05 arrival event; the first is 369 seconds later (dwell_start_offset_sec -369). The driver was not inside the pickup geofence when he tapped arrived, and his 07:38:40 message 'im at the phv bay' is contradicted by his own trace.

Once a limb of POL-NS-01 fails the fee is not chargeable at all, and POL-NS-06 makes the shortfall a full refund with no driver compensation payable, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied.

DRIVER ADVOCATE, ANSWERED. Your POL-NS-02 point is accepted so far as it goes: 25 qualifying fixes inside the 150 m hub radius exist, so the arrival test under POL-NS-02 is satisfied and the driver genuinely reached the bay — but that is precisely why the case turns on dwell, and the dwell is 236 s against 300 s. Your POL-NS-01(a)/(d) point is accepted; your POL-NS-01(b)/(c) reading is not, for the reasons above. Your amount point is accepted: $6.00 is the correct charge under the fee_schedule resolution rule, the GREATER of the TRANSPORT_HUB zone-class fee ($6.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee ($4.00), so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect — but a correctly computed amount does not make a non-chargeable fee chargeable. Your POL-NS-05 argument that the arrival marker stands is rejected: POL-NS-05 is not the only route to measuring the clock from GPS entry — POL-NS-01(c) does so itself — and in any event the recomputed dwell is the same 236 s, so POL-NS-05(i) would refund in full and POL-NS-05(ii)'s false-arrival referral does NOT fire because qualifying in-geofence fixes do exist. Your POL-NS-03 alternative is rejected: POL-NS-03 requires the driver to be stationary for the required dwell OUTSIDE the arrival radius but within 400 m; the driver's stationary fixes sit inside the 150 m radius at 30–92 m from the pin, and the required dwell was not served in any event, so no platform-funded goodwill ($3.00) arises. Your POL-NS-07/anti-farming point is accepted on its own terms — no_show_terminations_30d is 3 (below 4) and 3/88 = 0.034 (below 0.08), so the check does not trip — but compensation is not payable for a different reason: POL-NS-07 only pays where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not. Your POL-NS-09 escalation argument is rejected: the apparent conflict between a driver-set 'arrived' marker and the platform's trace is exactly what POL-NS-01(b) and POL-NS-02 are written to resolve (the marker is judged against the trace), and no limb of POL-NS-09 engages — confidence is well above the 0.70 floor, both profiles show disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0, the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 0, the anti-farming check does not trip, and no deciding artifact is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d).

RIDER ADVOCATE, ANSWERED. Your limb (b) and limb (c) failures are accepted and decide the case. Your POL-NS-06 point is accepted: the fee is refunded in full and no compensation is payable, and the $6.00 already returned is the correct disposition. Your POL-NS-06(i) point is accepted: the trace holds a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1, no excursions) and EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so no separate intervals can be summed and, under POL-NS-06(ii), a missing advisory never reduces the 300 s minimum. Your rider-presence point is accepted as a finding: all 88 rider fixes sit 50.5–91.7 m from the pin inside the 200 m hub radius, which is consistent with the rider's own account. Your POL-NS-08 clean-data point is accepted: the trace has no gaps (max_gap_sec 0.0), the arrival event falls within seconds of a GPS fix so no clock-skew limb is engaged, the chat log's 3 messages match trip_record.chat_message_count of 3, and the $6.00 line reconciles with the fee schedule. Your no-escalation point and your POL-GEN-03 point are accepted. One correction to your framing: because the FILING party here is the driver, the emitted ruling value is NO_ACTION, not FULL_REFUND — the outcome for the rider is the same (the refund stands), but POL-GEN-03 names the outcome for the filer.

CONFIDENCE AND EVIDENCE. The deciding facts — the 236-second in-geofence dwell and the absence of any qualifying in-radius fix at or before the arrival marker — are carried by EV-GPS-00209 and EV-TRIP-00209, and no artifact relied on is impaired under POL-NS-08(a)–(d), so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is not reduced. EV-ADVIS-00209-01 is absent (weight 0.0) and carries no fact; its absence only confirms that POL-NS-06(i) accumulation is unavailable. No profile field outside those POL-GEN-01 permits as a ground was used to decide anything. Confidence 0.90, above the 0.70 escalation floor.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and to the driver — this is a route-deviation case on trip TRP-00101, and both advocates actually converge on the same figures, which I accept.

Is the deviation established? Yes. The platform's GPS trace (EV-GPS-00101) records 27.18 km against the booked optimal of 21.0 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-00101) — an excess of 6.18 km, or 29.4%. Both of POL-RD-01's establishment gates pass (excess above 20% of optimal, and above 0.8 km absolute). The trace figure governs over the rounded trip-record copy of 27.2 km, as POL-RD-01 requires; nothing turns on the 0.02 km rounding. The trace is clean for POL-RD-07 purposes — 229 fixes, no gaps, max_gap 0.0 s, 10-second sampling — so no independent corroboration is needed to prove the excess, and the driver's own chat message MSG-00101-002 ('sorry boss missed the exit, coming back now') and his submitted statement confirm the navigation error anyway.

Does anything excuse it? No. There is no traffic advisory in the bundle (EV-ADVIS-00101-01 is empty), so POL-RD-03 cannot run. The rider requested no waypoint — every waypoint_hint is null and her message only objects to the route — so POL-RD-04 is unavailable. No endpoint was amended (POL-RD-05) and this is not a pooled trip (vehicle_type RYDE_X, solo_optimal null), so POL-RD-12 does not apply.

How much? The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs and the number is arithmetic, not discretionary. Reading the surge multiplier from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier (1.0): recomputed fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 21.0 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 27.63. Refund = 35.64 charged_total - 27.63 = 8.01, rounded UP to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 8.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de-minimis floor but only 22.5% of charged_total, well under the 90% full-refund share, so the ruling is PARTIAL_REFUND of 8.05, not the $10.00 the rider estimated by hand. There is no ERP, toll or surcharge line to add on top (erp_gantries empty, tolls 0.00, no airport surcharge), so POL-RD-09 makes no separate correction and nothing is double-counted. Driver compensation does not arise: the rider was billed 27.2 km against a 27.18 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall under POL-RD-04.

The materiality point both advocates raise is accepted: at 29.4% and 6.18 km this excess falls below BOTH of POL-RD-01's materiality thresholds (50% and 8.0 km), so it is not a MATERIAL deviation, the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check is not triggered, and no driver-conduct referral follows. Independently, the driver's trailing-90-day record shows 0 deviation flags across 812 completed trips (ratio 0.00), so no repeat pattern could be established even if the check had been required. No clause in the policy produces a referral on these facts, so the referrals list is empty.

Amount moved: 8.05 SGD to the rider. The present charge of 35.64 does not stand in full; 27.63 of it does.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).

To the rider and the driver:

What was claimed. The rider says the driver left the BKE for Mandai/Upper Thomson, that the trip took 32 minutes against a normal 27, and asks for $7.00 of the $29.91 metered fare back.

That the route changed is not really in dispute. The driver's own in-app message at 11:29:04 ("boss BKE quite jam, i go Upper Bukit Timah ok?") and his statement confirm he came off the booked corridor. But a route change is only a refundable deviation if it clears the gate in POL-RD-01, and this one does not.

The numbers. The governing distance is the GPS trace figure, not the trip record's rounded copy: trace_distance_km is 21.79 km (EV-GPS-00102), against the booked optimal of 20.4 km (EV-TRIP-00102, optimal_distance_km). The excess is 1.39 km, or 6.81% of the optimal distance. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be both more than 0.8 km in absolute terms AND more than 20% of the optimal distance (20% of 20.4 km is 4.08 km). Rider. I have considered and rejected your escalation argument. Here no clause was invoked and no artifact was cited; a bare traffic assertion is discarded under POL-RD-08, and POL-RD-03 was never reached because no deviation exists. Pattern. The driver's record shows 0 deviation flags in 90 days against 640 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no POL-RD-06 referral arises. No other clause produces a referral.
